purpose: Full one-cell occupiable tactical architecture, replacing flattened world-map symbols

prompts.fort: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single 16x16-pixel tactical map fort sprite for a humble retro fantasy strategy RPG, inspired by the simple readable NES Fire Emblem Gaiden terrain language. Create ONE complete miniature square stone watch-fort, frontal slightly top-down view, broad square silhouette almost equally tall and wide, two squat battlement shoulders and a central dark arch built into the facade, readable roof/courtyard top. It must fill a 16-by-16 logical tile almost edge-to-edge (15 pixels wide and 15 pixels tall) and represent a terrain square a soldier can occupy. All design is on an EXACT coarse 16x16 pixel grid, shown enlarged with perfectly flat hard square pixel blocks. Each logical pixel is one single solid colour, extremely limited 10-colour palette: warm dark grey stone #43443b, mossy grey #747564, pale stone #b0ac96, muted dark brown and black shadows, NO purple. Left/top lit. Build a substantial compact architectural silhouette, never a tiny horizontal map icon, never two disconnected tiny towers. Transparent background, isolated sprite, no floor square, no border, no grid lines, no text, no shadow outside silhouette, no gradients, no blur, no antialiasing, no realistic microtexture, no characters, no extra symbols. One design centered, ample transparent exterior.
